sourcedFrom: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip out of Staccato's own instructions: slide stop, slide forward off the frame, then the Dawson tool-less guide rod captured on its own takedown lever before the barrel comes out the front. The tool-less rod is the part that makes this different from a plain 1911 — it is captured deliberately, not compressed under your thumb.

steps.title: Unloaded, and the bench clear of ammunition
steps.action: Point it somewhere safe, drop the magazine, then lock the slide back and look into both the chamber and the magwell. Staccato asks for the work area itself to be free of ammunition, not just the pistol — a loose round on the bench is how a 'cleared' gun gets loaded again halfway through a strip.
steps.quote: Ensure your pistol is unloaded, and the work area is free of ammunition. Lock the slide back and visually inspect the chamber and magwell.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Takedown notch lined up with the slide stop knuckle
steps.action: Bring the slide back — not all the way to lock, but to where the takedown notch in the slide sits over the knuckle of the slide stop. Hold it there. If the notch is not aligned the slide stop will not start out, and forcing it is how the frame gets scarred.
steps.quote: Move the slide back to align the takedown notch with the slide stop knuckle.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Slide stop pressed from the right and drawn out
steps.action: Push on the protruding end of the slide stop from the right side of the pistol with a fingertip or a small tool, and draw it out to the left with the other hand. It should start with light pressure once the notch is aligned — if it needs force, the slide has moved off the notch.
steps.quote: Press on the slide stop from the opposite side with your finger or a small tool and remove the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 3

steps.title: Slide run forward off the frame
steps.action: With the slide stop out, run the whole top end forward off the frame rails and set the frame aside. Keep it level as it comes off — tipping it lets the recoil assembly start out of the slide before you have captured it.
steps.quote: Pull the slide forward and off the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 4

steps.title: Guide rod flange pushed forward to expose the takedown lever
steps.action: Push forward on the flange at the rear of the guide rod. That compresses the spring just far enough to bring the small takedown lever on the Dawson tool-less rod out where you can reach it. This is the step that replaces a 1911's plug-and-bushing wrestle, and it is why no bushing wrench appears anywhere in this procedure.
steps.quote: Push forward on the guide rod flange to expose the takedown lever on the Dawson toolless guide rod.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Takedown lever lowered onto the reverse plug to capture the spring
steps.action: Press the lever down and let it come to rest on the edge of the reverse plug. That is what holds the recoil system captured as one unit. Do not let the flange slip forward while you are doing this — the spring is under load and an uncaptured rod will launch.
steps.caution: The recoil spring is compressed at this point and is held only by that lever resting on the plug. Keep control of the flange until you feel the lever seat.
steps.quote: Press the takedown lever and lower it so that it rests on the edge of the reverse plug.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 6

steps.title: Captured recoil system out through the rear of the slide
steps.action: With the lever holding it captured, lift the whole recoil assembly out of the slide rearward — out through the back, not the muzzle. It comes away as one piece and stays that way for cleaning.
steps.quote: Remove the captured system from the slide out through the back.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 7

steps.title: Link flipped forward, barrel out the muzzle end
steps.action: Flip the barrel link forward toward the muzzle so it clears, then slide the barrel out through the front of the slide. That is the strip — frame, slide, captured recoil assembly and barrel. Anything further is not in Staccato's published procedure.
steps.quote: Slide the barrel link forward and slide it out through the front of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato P Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 8

deepAbsentReason: Staccato publishes this page as basic disassembly and reassembly — the article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato P', and it ends at barrel, slide, frame and the captured recoil assembly. There is no extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip-module procedure published anywhere on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. Staccato's own instruction for anything beyond what is written is to contact their Customer Service directly, which is what the page gives an address for. Nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush the bore from breech to muzzle, repeating as many times as it takes
Oil the bore after cleaning, then run a patch through to take the excess back out
Leave a film, not a wet bore — excess oil in a chamber raises pressure and collects carbon

cleaning.name: BARREL & SLIDE EXTERIOR
tasks: Brush debris off the outside of the barrel and off the slide
Wipe the breech face and under the extractor claw
Wipe the barrel's lugs and the link

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR (IF FITTED)
tasks: Scrape and brush carbon build-up out of the inside of the comp
Apply a thin layer of CLP to the inside of the comp
Staccato marks this step IF APPLICABLE — a P without a comp skips it entirely

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Wipe the captured recoil assembly and check the spring for kinks before it goes back

reassembly: Check the barrel link is flipped forward, then feed the barrel back in through the front of the slide.
Insert the guide rod and push on the rear of the flange to release the takedown lever, lowering it gently into place.

Line the slide rails up on the frame and run the slide back on. Staccato's own note: the guide rod flange must be pushed up against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must not be rotated to either side, or the top end will not go fully on.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the slide stop's pin has to pass through the link or the pistol will not function. If the hole is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the slide stop knuckle, then seat the slide stop fully.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery, check the slide stop is fully seated flush and that it locks the slide back on an empty magazine, and confirm the thumb and grip safeties both function before handling.
